text.text_excerpt: This place is great. The kitchen in the back of the store has different meals and specials every day. The carne asada which is made to order and served with beans rice, tortilla & salad, is $7 and it's delicious. Tacos are also awesome. The bakery has a bunch of desserts; but I specially love their "tres leches" yummmy!. They also have a small supermarket with all kinds of CentralAmerican staples.

This is an interesting place. They call themselves a "bakery", but it's more a small grocery that offers a whole array of things. Me and some friends we starving and having been here before, they said this was a good place to get some Mexican Food. Walking in, I honestly had no idea what was going on. We walked to the back where there was a menu taped up and food being prepared. A lot of people didn't speak English, so I was a little intimidated. Looking over the menu, I thought that the beef quesadilla sounded good and for $7, it seemed like a good deal for lunch. I ordered and waited. When you get your food, it comes with a ticket and you pay at the register in front of the store. Just ...

After driving past this place so many times, we decided to stop in, and I'm glad that we did. My husband said the burrito was the closest he's had in NOLA to the San Diego ones that he misses. It was $6 with rice and beans and carne asada. The ingredients were very fresh. While we waited, one of the owners offered us warm white cheese on a tortilla. It was yummy. I cannot recall what he called it, but he was very nice. He said that many days they will do a cooked meat special and that if we ever need a pork shoulder for a party that this is the place to go. The desserts looked tasty and interesting. Definitely want to try some more things here.
